seoTitle: Currency Converter - Live Foreign Exchange Rates
metaDescription: Free currency converter. Convert between USD, EUR, GBP, JPY, and all major global currencies using live, up-to-date foreign exchange rates.
intro: Whether you are traveling abroad, shopping on an international website, or sending money overseas, knowing the exact exchange rate is essential. Our free Currency Converter provides instant, accurate conversions between all major global currencies. Using up-to-date foreign exchange rates, you can easily calculate how much your money is worth in US Dollars, Euros, British Pounds, Japanese Yen, and dozens of other fiat currencies.
whatIs: A currency converter is a financial tool that translates the value of one currency into the corresponding value of another currency. It relies on the Foreign Exchange (Forex) market, where currencies are traded globally 24 hours a day. Because these rates fluctuate constantly based on global economics, interest rates, and geopolitical events, a live converter is necessary to get the most accurate valuation.
howToUse: Enter the Amount you wish to convert.
Select the Base Currency (the money you have) from the dropdown list.
Select the Target Currency (the money you want) from the dropdown list.
Click 'Convert' to instantly see the equivalent amount in the target currency.
howItWorks: The tool retrieves the current exchange rate between the two selected currencies. It multiplies the amount you entered by the exchange rate. For example, if the USD to EUR rate is 0.92, converting $100 means multiplying 100 by 0.92, giving you 92 Euros. The underlying rates are typically updated daily or hourly from major financial data providers.
workedExample: You want to buy a product listed at 150 British Pounds (£) and you need to know the cost in US Dollars ($). You enter 150, select GBP as the base currency, and USD as the target. If the current GBP to USD exchange rate is 1.25, the calculator multiplies 150 × 1.25. The result is $187.50. You now know the exact cost in your local currency.
resultInterpretation: The result displays the converted amount based on the mid-market exchange rate. This is the 'true' rate banks use to trade with one another. When you actually exchange physical money or use a credit card abroad, the rate you receive may be slightly worse because banks and currency exchanges add a markup or spread to make a profit.
useCases: Travel Budgeting: Calculate how much local currency you will get for your holiday spending money.
Online Shopping: Determine the true cost of an item priced in a foreign currency before buying.
International Remittances: Check the baseline rate before sending money to family overseas to ensure you get a fair deal.
Business Invoicing: Convert invoice amounts when billing international clients.
Forex Trading: Quickly check currency pairs for trading or investment purposes.
tipsAndLimitations: The rate shown is the 'mid-market' rate. Consumer exchange rates at airports, banks, or via PayPal will include hidden markups.
Exchange rates fluctuate constantly during the trading week. A rate checked on Friday may change by Monday.
Credit cards often charge a Foreign Transaction Fee (typically 1% to 3%) on top of the exchange rate. Check your card's terms.
When traveling, it is usually better to let your bank do the conversion by withdrawing from an ATM rather than using airport exchange kiosks.

faq.question: What is the mid-market rate?
faq.answer: The mid-market rate is the midpoint between the buy and sell prices of two currencies. It is considered the fairest, 'real' exchange rate.

faq.question: Why is the rate I got at the bank different?
faq.answer: Banks and exchange bureaus add a profit margin (a markup) to the mid-market rate, which is why their rates are worse for consumers.

faq.question: How often are the rates updated?
faq.answer: Our calculator uses rates that are updated frequently throughout the trading day to ensure high accuracy.

faq.question: Is it better to exchange money before or during travel?
faq.answer: It is generally best to avoid airport kiosks. Withdrawing local currency from an ATM at your destination usually offers a rate much closer to the mid-market rate.
